warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/oracle/PriceFeed.sol#L63-L77


# Vulnerability details

## Bug Description 
The `PriceFeed` contract has sequencerUptimeFeed checks in place to assert if the sequencer on an L2 is running but these checks are not implemented correctly. The [chainlink docs ](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds)say that `sequencerUptimeFeed` can return a 0 value for `startedAt` if it is called during an "invalid round". 

![0A5A6D3A-C8EA-46CF-810C-88AA0C420803_4_5005_c](https://github.com/adeolu98/text-me-anon/assets/39372980/75166f79-13d9-457a-841b-394eae9ba468)

Please note that an **"invalid round"** is described to mean there was a problem updating the sequencer's status, possibly due to network issues or problems with data from oracles, and is shown by a `startedAt` time of 0 and `answer` is 0. Further explanation can be seen as given by an official chainlink engineer as seen here in the chainlink public discord

https://discord.com/channels/592041321326182401/605768708266131456/1213847312141525002
![D381502F-BE29-4A78-BEA7-63BB4D277886_4_5005_c](https://github.com/adeolu98/text-me-anon/assets/39372980/50bc2d7a-d8ef-4e74-947f-9c25b45126ca)



This makes the implemented check below in the [PriceFeed.getPrice()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/oracle/PriceFeed.sol#L63C1-L82C6) to be useless if its called in an invalid round. 

```solidity
            if (block.timestamp - startedAt <= GRACE_PERIOD_TIME) { 
                revert Errors.GRACE_PERIOD_NOT_OVER();
            }
```
as startedAt will be 0, the arithmetic operation block.timestamp - startedAt will result in a value greater than GRACE_PERIOD_TIME (which is hardcoded to be 3600) i.e block.timestamp = 1719739032, so 1719739032 - 0 = 1719739032 which is bigger than 3600. The code won't revert.


Imagine a case where a round starts, at the beginning `startedAt` is recorded to be 0, and  `answer`, the initial status is set to be 0. Note that docs say that if `answer` = 0, sequencer is up, if equals to 1, sequencer is down. But in this case here, `answer` and `startedAt` can be 0 initially, till after all data is gotten from oracles and update is confirmed then the values are reset to the correct values that show the correct status of the sequencer.  

From these explanations and information, it can be seen that `startedAt` value is a second value that should be used in the check for if a sequencer is down/up or correctly updated. The checks in [PriceFeed.getPrice()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/oracle/PriceFeed.sol#L63C1-L82C6) will allow for sucessfull calls in an invalid round because reverts dont happen if answer == 0 and startedAt == 0 thus defeating the purpose of having a sequencerFeed check to assertain the status of the sequencerFeed on L2 i.e if it is up/down/active or if its status is actually confirmed to be either. 

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/oracle/PriceFeed.sol#L68C1-L76C14
```solidity
            if (answer == 1) {
                // sequencer is down
                revert Errors.SEQUENCER_DOWN();
            }

            if (block.timestamp - startedAt <= GRACE_PERIOD_TIME) {
                // time since up
                revert Errors.GRACE_PERIOD_NOT_OVER();
            }
```

## Impact
inadequate checks to confirm the correct status of the sequecncer/sequecncerUptimeFeed in `PriceFeed.getPrice()` contract will cause `getPrice()` to not revert even when the sequcncer uptime feed is not updated or is called in an invalid round.  


## Tools Used
manual review 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
add a check that reverts if `startedAt` is returned as 0.






## Assessed type

Oracle

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Liquidate.sol#L18


# Vulnerability details

## Bug Description 

The liquidation function `liquidate()` doesn't have a deadline parameter meaning  it is  susceptible to certain MEV attacks. As liquidation involves reading price from an [oracle](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/RiskLibrary.sol#L57) to determine if the position is [underwater/unhealthy](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Liquidate.sol#L44), a liquidation call for an unhealthy position can be manipulated in a way by a third party MEV actor that it gets delayed until the position becomes healthy again i.e when the oracle returns a better price. This then makes the liquidation call revert as it is now healthy and is not liquidatable. 

This manipulation will be enticing to MEV actors who have bias towards certain low health positions during high price-volatility periods. 

This griefs the liquidator as collateral profit which the liquidator should have rightly collected at that time/instant when the liquidation call was sent cannot be collected anymore because of a third party manipulation on-chain.  

The liquidator should be allowed to specify how long a liquidation call is valid for to make things fair. 

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Liquidate.sol#L18-L23

```solidity
struct LiquidateParams {
    // The debt position ID to liquidate
    uint256 debtPositionId;
    // The minimum profit in collateral tokens expected by the liquidator
    uint256 minimumCollateralProfit;
}
```
Snippet of the `liquidate()` call parameters which show the absence of a user specified deadline parameter. 

## Impact
absence of deadline parameter in the `liqudate()` function and its dependence on volatile asset price makes it susceptible to MEV manipulation. 

## Tools used 
manual review 

## Recommended Mitigation
let liquidators specify a tx deadline for their calls

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Initialize.sol#L237


# Vulnerability details

## Bug Description 
![3307DF49-DF7E-4952-805E-7BFB9925CB9F_4_5005_c](https://github.com/adeolu98/audits-draft/assets/39372980/9de4f218-9258-486e-b15f-c9d1b3237739)

According to the aave docs, see [here](https://docs.aave.com/developers/core-contracts/pooladdressesprovider), the pool address should not be hardcoded, and instead the PoolAddressProvider contract should be queried EVERYTIME to provide the current pool address. This is because **if the pool contract is to be migrated to a new address**, it will break the Size protocol contract and force a redeploy/upgrade/change of implementation as the address is set once via `executeInitializeData()` as seen [here](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Initialize.sol#L237) and there is no way to change the set aave pool adddress in storage.

The PoolAddressProvider contract never changes and will always provide the latest pool address when queried.

in the `PoolAddressProvider`, there is a function that allows the AAVE admins to change the POOL address returned by [PoolAddressProvider.getPool()](https://github.com/aave/aave-v3-core/blob/6070e82d962d9b12835c88e68210d0e63f08d035/contracts/protocol/configuration/PoolAddressesProvider.sol#L75) at any time. see [here](https://github.com/aave/aave-v3-core/blob/6070e82d962d9b12835c88e68210d0e63f08d035/contracts/protocol/configuration/PoolAddressesProvider.sol#L57)

The current implementation in Size goes against the aave integration recommendations, as it is not fetched whenever needed but instead set once and can never be updated in the case of a change. 


# Impact
Aave pools not integrated correctly, aave pool address hardcoded which is against aave pool integration guidelines. Aave pool update to a different address will force redeploy/upgrade Size inplementation contract. 

## Tools used 
manual review 

## Recommended Mitigation
always get the pool address from the aave pool address provider contract before every call to the pool.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/main/src/Size.sol#L1


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The extra rewards earned by liquidity providers are locked within the protocol (address(size)) and are not able to be claimed, resulting in a loss of potential yield for users.

## Proof of Concept
Like many other lending protocols, Aave distributes additional rewards to users to incentivize supplying liquidity and, in some cases, borrowing. This is especially prevalent on L2 chains, where the chain itself may offer significant rewards (high APYs) for liquidity providers.

However, the size protocol does not provide any mechanism to claim these earned rewards, effectively locking them within the protocol.

According to the Aave documentation (https://docs.aave.com/developers/whats-new/multiple-rewards-and-claim), extra rewards are managed by the Aave RewardsController (https://docs.aave.com/developers/periphery-contracts/rewardscontroller). And users can call `rewardcontroller.claimRewards(assets, amount, to, reward)` to claim a single reward type.

## Recommendation
We understand that adding the functionality to distribute rewards to users may introduce significant complexity to the protocol's internal accounting and require substantial development effort. 

However, we believe the protocol should, at a minimum, implement a function to claim the rewards and transfer them to the `feeRecipient`. These claimed rewards could then be either distributed as a protocol fee or used to bolster the protocol's insurance fund to handle bad debt.

Adding an admin function like `claimRewardsFromAAVE(address Rewardstoken)` would be relatively straightforward to implement. It would ensure that the rightfully earned rewards do not remain locked and unusable within the protocol.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/Size.sol#L198


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The size protocol offer fixed interest loan that are due in some point in the future. In the case that the `creditPosition.duedate` is reached and the borrower didn't pay then the loan, the `debtPosition becomes elligible for liquidations and the liquidators will get  incintivised to liquidate the positon.
The protocol uses the oz pause library to allow for pausing the prtocol, in the case of a risk or a security incident.  

The problem however arises, from the fact that the protocol doesn't put a safeguard in place in the case that during the period of the pause, that some debtPosition have matured and became elligible for liquidations. 
## Proof of Concept
Protocol admins are able to pause and unpause the protocol by calling `pause()` and `unpause()`. and in the case that the protocol is paused all the user facing functions would be unavailable and will fail (they are all equipped with `whenNotPaused` which will revert if protocol paused). This would block users from being able to repay their debt, before they become overddue and raced on to be liquidated by MEV Bots

**Example Scenario**

1. Alice takes out a loan of 1000 USDC from the Size protocol, with a due date set for June 30th.
2. On June 29th, the protocol is paused by the admins due to a potential security risk.
3. Alice's loan becomes overdue on June 30th while the protocol is still paused.
4. On July 1st, the protocol is unpaused.
5. Immediately after the protocol is unpaused, liquidators (potentially MEV bots) identify Alice's overdue debt position and liquidate it.
6. Alice loses her collateral and faces a liquidation penalty, despite being unable to repay her loan during the pause period.


## Recomendation
We recommend adding a mechanism to create something like a `grace period` where liquidation are blocked for 1-2 hours  while repayment, deposit and all operations that improve the health of positions are enabled. This will lead to more stability in the protocol and to avoid times when the debt becomes overdue but the protocol was paused and the positions get liquidated

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/SizeStorage.sol#L16


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The size protocol is expected to be deployed on mainnet where the gas fees could range from 5 usd to 40 USDC, it might be important especially for lenders to decide the minamount of their Liquidity provided to be lent out in a CreditPosition, as the cost to claim those Positions could eat out at their yield. Please also note, as it is the case now, lenders are required to call the `claim()` function in order for their lent out assets to be accredited to their account in order to be lent out. 
> N.B please also note that the protocol has put in a place a `fragmentationFee` to disentivize credit traders from fragmenting creditPositions (later streamlined to be claimed by the bot), However this fragmentation fee wouldn't help if the creditPosition created first is itself really small   
## Proof Of Concept
- User: Alice
- Initial Liquidity Provided: 1000 USDC
- Minimum Debt Amount(Protocol): 50 USDC
- Gas Fee per Transaction on Eth mainnet: 15 USDC
- Annual Percentage Yield  set by alice (APY): 7%

#### Attack Execution
1. **Griefer Action**: A griefer opens multiple limit orders, each with the minimum debt amount of 50 USDC.
2. **Fragmentation**: Alice's 1000 USDC is fragmented into 20 separate positions of 50 USDC each.
3. Alice needs to call the `claim()` function to retrieve her lent out assets.
4. Each `claim()` call costs 15 USDC in gas fees. (could be batched together, but we are focusing on worst case now)

**Calculation of Loss**  
- Total Gas Fees: 20 positions * 15 USDC = 300 USDC
- Yield from Lending: 7% APY on 1000 USDC = 70 USDC per year.
- If Alice claims her positions within a year, the gas fees (300 USDC) far exceed the yield (70 USDC).

**Result**  
- **Total Yield**: 70 USDC
- **Total Gas Fees**: 300 USDC
- **Net Loss**: 300 USDC (gas fees) - 70 USDC (yield) = 230 USDC

## Recomendation
The perfect solution, that we would recommend to such a problem is to add a user define risk parameter `minCreditAmount` and to use `max(UserConfig.minCreditAmount,RiskConfig.minimumCreditBorrowAToken)` to validate the minimum size of newly opened position for the user. This way the users could chose which minimum Credit Amount they are okay with, considering multiple factors such as the APY and the desired maturity duration of the positions.





## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/main/src/libraries/actions/BuyCreditMarket.sol#L162


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
A lender’s creditpositionid can be bought by another lender. If the new apr is bigger than the previous apr when a new lender buys the previous lender’s creditpositionid, then the previous lender will lose some borrowAmount.

## Proof of Concept
1. Let’s assume, Alice(borrower) creates a borrow offer with 3 months(5% apr), 4 months(6% apr), 5 months(7% apr). bob(another user) also creates a borrow offer with 3 months(8% apr), 4 months(9% apr), 5 months(10% apr).

2. Now Bob calls the function buyCreditMarket with Alice as borrower,  5 months(7% apr) as tenor, amount 100e18,  exactAmountIn is  true on January 1st. 

3. Now a creditPositionId(assume id is 1) is created and its lender is bob,  borrower is alice, futureValue is 107  ,  dueDate is june 1 and forSale: true.

4. After 2 months , john calls the function buyCreditMarket with amount 99.07e18,  exactAmountIn is  true and creditPositionId is 1 to buy the creditPositionId.

5. See  function executeBuyCreditMarket, as here params.creditPositionId is not equal to  RESERVED_ID, so here  borrower = creditPosition.lender = bob, tenor = debtPosition.dueDate - block.timestamp = 3 months. Bob’s 3 months(tenor) apr is 8%(see bob’s borrow offer above).

6. As params.exactAmountIn is true, the getCreditAmountOut function is called with cashAmountIn = 99.07e18, maxCashAmountIn = 99.07e18, maxCredit = 107e18. getCreditAmountOut function, as cashAmountIn is equal to maxCashAmountIn, so the getCreditAmountOut returns creditAmountOut = 107e18. Now creditPositionId 1’s lender is john and credit is 107e18.

7.  The problem is the previous lender(Bob) gets 99.07e18(ignore fees) borrowAToken but Bob should get more than 100e18  borrowAToken with profit.


## Tools Used
manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Make sure apr should be bigger than previous lender’s apr when a  lender buy creditpositionid from another lender. 




## Assessed type

Other

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/main/src/libraries/actions/SetUserConfiguration.sol#L50


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

When a creditpositionid is opened for a user. By default  the creditpositionid forSale is true. User can make forSale false for individual creditpositionid or user can  disable  allCreditPositions Sale by calling the  function setUserConfiguration. But the problem is the user can’t make allCreditPositionsForSaleDisabled true if he has no creditpositionid.so when a creditpositionid is opened for the 1st time for a user, by default  forSale is true. If the user’s intention is not to sell the creditpositionid , he has to  make forSale  false/allCreditPositionsForSaleDisabled  true after opening the creditposition. But the attacker can frontrun and buy the creditposition before making it forSale - false. This may make users get less profit.

## Proof of Concept
1. Let’s assume, Alice creates borrow offer with 3 months(3% apr), 4 months(4% apr), 5 months(5% apr).

2. bob(lender) calls the function buyCreditMarket with alice as borrower and 3  months(3% apr) as tenor.this is bob’s 1st creditpositonid, so by default forSale is true. Bob’s intention is to make forSale false for this creditposition.

3. Before bob making forSale false for this creditposition, john frontruns and buy the creditpositionid

## Tools Used
manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make sure that before creating any creditpositionid , the user can make allCreditPositionsForSaleDisabled true.





## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/main/src/libraries/actions/Compensate.sol#L139


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
When compensating a creditposition with another creditposition(borrower  creditposition), there is no check whether the creditposition forSale - false/true. As a result lender creditposition(after replacing with new creditposition ) other lenders without their intention before making forSale - false for the creditposition.



## Proof of Concept
1. Let’s assume, alice has 3 creditpositionid . they are creditpositionid 1, creditpositionid 2, creditpositionid 3.

2. Alice’s creditpositionid 2’s debtpositionid is 2 whose borrower is bob.

3. Alice’s creditpositionid 2’s borrower is Bob who has also 3 creditpositionid and those are  creditpositionid 4, creditpositionid 5, creditpositionid 6.

4. Bob wants to compensate for debt with his creditposition. So Bob compensated debt of creditposition 2 by giving creditposition 4 to alice. 

5. Here Alice's  creditpositionid 2’s forSale - false but Bob's creditposition 4’s  forSale - true. Now alice gets creditposition 4 which forSale is true which is unintentional for alice.

## Tools Used
manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
When compensating , replace forSale condition from old creditpositionid to new creditpositioid for lenders.





## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/test/BaseTest.sol#L1-L411


# Vulnerability details

### Report on `CreateInitCodeSizeLimit` Issue and Potential Optimizations for the Size Protocol

**Finding Category**: Gas Optimization / Library Issues

**Description**:

During the deployment of contracts for the Size protocol, an error `Invalid transaction: CreateInitCodeSizeLimit` was encountered. This error indicates that the size of the initialization code for the contract exceeds the block gas limit allowed by the Ethereum network. Here are the detailed observations and potential solutions:

#### Problem

The error `Invalid transaction: CreateInitCodeSizeLimit` occurs when the combined size of the contract's bytecode and the initialization code exceeds the maximum allowed size. This can result from large contracts with complex logic or multiple levels of inheritance.

#### Observations

1. **Contract Size**: The contract being deployed appears to be too large, potentially due to extensive use of libraries and complex logic.
2. **Library Usage**: Multiple libraries are being linked during the deployment, which increases the overall size of the contract.
3. **Inheritance**: Deep inheritance chains can contribute to increased contract size.

#### Potential Solutions

To address the `CreateInitCodeSizeLimit` issue and optimize gas usage, the following strategies are recommended:

1. **Optimize Contracts**:
   - **Remove Unused Code**: Ensure that contracts do not contain unnecessary code or imports.
   - **Efficient Library Usage**: Use libraries efficiently to reduce redundant code.
   - **Flatten Inheritance**: Consider flattening the inheritance structure or removing unnecessary levels of inheritance.

2. **Split the Contract**:
   - Break the contract into smaller, modular contracts that interact with each other. This can help keep the deployment size within limits.

3. **Use Constructor Arguments**:
   - Reduce the size of the constructor by passing some of the initialization data as arguments, which can be set after deployment if necessary.

#### Mathematical Justification

To quantify the effect of optimizations, we use the following gas cost formulas:

$$
\text{Total Gas Cost} = \text{Base Gas Cost} + \sum_{i=1}^{n} \text{Library Gas Cost}_i + \text{Contract Initialization Gas Cost}
$$

Where:
- \(\text{Base Gas Cost}\) is the fixed gas cost for contract deployment.
- \(\text{Library Gas Cost}_i\) is the gas cost associated with each linked library.
- \(\text{Contract Initialization Gas Cost}\) is the gas cost for initializing the contract state.

By optimizing the contract and reducing the size of the bytecode and initialization code, the \(\text{Contract Initialization Gas Cost}\) can be significantly reduced, leading to a lower total gas cost.

---

In the Ethereum network, if a transaction fails due to an error such as `CreateInitCodeSizeLimit`, the gas used for processing up to the point of failure is consumed and not refunded. By implementing these optimizations, the deployment process can be streamlined, and the Size protocol contracts can be deployed within the permissible gas limits.

```
truffle develop
```

```
npx hardhat node
```

title: Unexpected reverts or no incentives during liquidation due to wrong liquidatorReward calculation.
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Liquidate.sol#L95-L100


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
* Unexpected DOS in every ```executeLiquidate``` function call even when the liquidator set a valid ```minimumCollateralProfit```.
* Incase the liquidator doesn't set any ```minimumCollateralProfit``` he only gets dust amount of collaterlTokens as reward. 
* No incentives leads to less competition which increases the risk of protocol incurring bad debt or lenders taking a loss. So, the protocol bots are the only entity that will likely call ```executeLiquidate``` in this case. And they will be forced to spend more than the rewards earned to keep up with every liquidation. 
* this will also affect the ```liquidateWithReplacement```.

## Proof of Concept
During liquidations we see that the ```liquidatorReward``` is calculated and added to ```liquidatorProfitCollateralToken``` and then sent to the liquidator as an award for calling ```executeLiquidate```. :
```javascript
// profitable liquidation
        if (assignedCollateral > debtInCollateralToken) {
            uint256 liquidatorReward = Math.min(
                assignedCollateral - debtInCollateralToken,
                Math.mulDivUp(debtPosition.futureValue, state.feeConfig.liquidationRewardPercent, PERCENT)
            );
            liquidatorProfitCollateralToken = debtInCollateralToken + liquidatorReward;
```

```javascript
 state.data.collateralToken.transferFrom(debtPosition.borrower, msg.sender, liquidatorProfitCollateralToken);
```

But if we look closely at ```Math.mulDivUp(debtPosition.futureValue, state.feeConfig.liquidationRewardPercent, PERCENT)```, it uses ```debtPosition.futureValue``` to calculate the reward and sent it as ```collateralToken```. This is wrong because ```debtPosition.futureValue``` is in 1e6 precision and the ```collateralToken``` is in 1e18 precision which means we are basically sending dust amount of collateralTokens as a reward everytime a liquidation is done. 


Also, the ```liquidatorReward``` is assigned by choosing the minimum value between, ```assignedCollateral - debtInCollateralToken``` and ```Math.mulDivUp(debtPosition.futureValue, state.feeConfig.liquidationRewardPercent, PERCENT)```.
Comparing them will always give us ```liquidatorReward``` = ```Math.mulDivUp(debtPosition.futureValue, state.feeConfig.liquidationRewardPercent, PERCENT)``` because the first one is in 1e18 precision and the second one is in 1e6 precision. Obviously the second one will always be chosen over the first one, even when the first value is very less.




Example, a position with 1_000_000 debt is liquidated;

```liquidatorReward``` = ```1_000_000e6 * 0.05e18 * 1e18``` = ```50000e6```.
This seems like a valid reward for liquidating a position with 1 million ```debtToken``` but this is added to ```liquidatorProfitCollateralToken = debtInCollateralToken + liquidatorReward;``` and is sent as ```collateralToken```. 


Since ```5000e6``` is still in futureValue precision(1e6) but is sent as ```collateralToken``` which is in 1e18 precision, ```5000e6``` as collateralToken will only amount to less than a dollar in current collateralToken price. 

See: [ethereum unit converter](https://eth-converter.com/) by putting 5000e6 wei we get 0 dollars current value.

If even a very large position(1 million) rewards only ```50000e6``` = ```0.00000005e18``` collateralToken = ```$ 0.00``` dollars. The reward for smaller positions will only get lesser.  
```
Position             Reward in collateraToken
                       
100_000              0.000000005e18   
10_000               0.0000000005e18 
1000                 0.00000000005e18 
100                  0.000000000005e18
...                  ...
all worth 0 dollars. 
```


## Tools Used
manual 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Make sure to use the converted value of ```position.futureValue``` during collateralToken reward calculation. 
```diff
        if (assignedCollateral > debtInCollateralToken) {
            uint256 liquidatorReward = Math.min(
                assignedCollateral - debtInCollateralToken,
-               Math.mulDivUp(debtPosition.futureValue, state.feeConfig.liquidationRewardPercent, PERCENT)
+               Math.mulDivUp(debtInCollateralToken, state.feeConfig.liquidationRewardPercent, PERCENT)
            ); 
```








## Assessed type

Decimal

raw_row.title: Protocol swap fees accidentally sent to lender instead of the protocol due to wrong fees calculation in SellCreditMarket.

title: Protocol swap fees accidentally sent to lender instead of the protocol due to wrong fees calculation in SellCreditMarket.
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/SellCreditMarket.sol#L168-L181
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/AccountingLibrary.sol#L228-L263


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Whenever a ```SellCreditMarket``` is executed with ```params.exactAmountIn``` = ```false```, some amount of protocol swap fees will always be sent to the lender instead of the protocol.

Meaning whenever a borrower borrows cash, or when a credit owner sells his credit to exit cash early, some portion of swap fees always goes to the credit buyer(lender incase of borrowing). 

## Proof of Concept
Example,
a borrower wants to borrow 1000 USDC using ```SellCreditMarket``` any say fee is 5% APR and tenor is 5 years, then ratePerTenor = 20%. So, he calls it with ```RESERVED_ID``` and ```exactAmountIn = false``` because he wants to borrow exactly 1000 cash.
```javascript
} else {
            cashAmountOut = params.amount;

            (creditAmountIn, fees) = state.getCreditAmountIn({
                cashAmountOut: cashAmountOut,
                maxCashAmountOut: params.creditPositionId == RESERVED_ID
                    ? cashAmountOut
                    : Math.mulDivDown(creditPosition.credit, PERCENT - state.getSwapFeePercent(tenor), PERCENT + ratePerTenor),
                maxCredit: params.creditPositionId == RESERVED_ID
                    ? Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, PERCENT + ratePerTenor, PERCENT - state.getSwapFeePercent(tenor))
                    : creditPosition.credit,
                ratePerTenor: ratePerTenor,
                tenor: tenor
            });
        }
```
creditAmountIn and fees are calculated using ```getCreditAmountIn``` 
```javascript
if (cashAmountOut == maxCashAmountOut) {
            // no credit fractionalization

            creditAmountIn = maxCredit;
            fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT)
```

Now, we have ratePerTenor = 0.2e18(20%) and swapFeePercent = 0.1e18(10%). 
We get:
* cashAmountOut = 1000
* creditAmountIn = 1334
* fees = 100
* Positions are created with the calculated amounts.

This means the borrower has to pay 1334 back for borrowing 1000 at 20%. 
Here, we do not get ```creditAmountIn = 1200``` because the fees are to be paid by the cash reciever(borrower) and in this case, the borrower is also borrowing the fees and hence 20% for each borrowed fees.
```javascript
state.data.borrowAToken.transferFrom(params.lender, msg.sender, cashAmountOut); 
        state.data.borrowAToken.transferFrom(params.lender, state.feeConfig.feeRecipient, fees); 
        //@audit fees are paid by the lender at the time of execution so the borrower has to pay back the fees along with its interest accrued
```
When ```fees = 100``` is borrowed, think it of as a new borrow execution, then interest have to be paid to lender, and also swap fees need to be taken which is ```fees = 10% of 100 = 10```. 
And for this ```fees = 10``` is also to be borrowed. 
So, when a borrow is done with ```amount = cash```, it means the each fees taken are subsequent borrows.

See [docs](https://docs.size.credit/technical-docs/contracts/3.3-market-orders#:~:text=the%20credit%20seller-,With,to%20be%20sold%20to%20get%20the%20desired%20amount%20out,-3.3.2%20Buy%20Credit) for better explaination on ```creditAmountIn``` calculation.

Interest to be paid to lender on each subsequent borrows(fee is also borrowed) is calculated correctly but the fees calculation only include the fees for the first borrowed amount and the rest are ignored. 

```fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT)```

Keep in mind that even though the fees for subsequent borrows are ignored while calculating fees, it is still paid by the borrower and is already included in the ```creditAmountIn``` calculation, so it means the lender recieves the ignored fees.


The correct fees calculation should be:
```
at 10% fees ;
-----------------------------------------------
fees for first borrow(amount borrowed = 1000)
    = 10% of 1000
    = 100
-----------------------------------------------
since 100 is also borrowed and so on 
fees on second borrow(amount borrowed = 100)
    = 10% of 100
    = 10
-----------------------------------------------
fees on third borrow(amount borrowed = 10)
    = 10% of 10
    = 1
-----------------------------------------------
Total fees = 100 + 10 + 1
           = 111

```
But the function returns only 100 for fees, this means 11 amount of fees for the protocol went to the lender instead. Because it is already included in the ```credtiAmountIn```.
OR precisely in e16 precision: 11111111 - 10000000 = 1111111 


To prove this, lets do the opposite i.e. borrower calls ```SellCreditAmount``` with ```exactAmountIn``` = false, indicating he wants to repay the exact credit amount specified and calculate the amount of cash he recieves. 
Lets call this with ```amount = 1334```, so that ```creditAmouintIn = 1334``` exactly the same as our example.
Now, with 20% ratePerTenor and 10% fees we get;
```javascript
if (params.exactAmountIn) { 
            creditAmountIn = params.amount; // 1334

            (cashAmountOut, fees) = state.getCashAmountOut({
                creditAmountIn: creditAmountIn, // 1334
                maxCredit: params.creditPositionId == RESERVED_ID ? creditAmountIn :  creditPosition.credit,
                ratePerTenor: ratePerTenor,
                tenor: tenor
            });
```
```javascript
 function getCashAmountOut(
        State storage state,
        uint256 creditAmountIn,
        uint256 maxCredit,
        uint256 ratePerTenor,
        uint256 tenor
    ) internal view returns (uint256 cashAmountOut, uint256 fees) {
        uint256 maxCashAmountOut = Math.mulDivDown(creditAmountIn, PERCENT, PERCENT + ratePerTenor);
                                 //@audit 1334 * 1e18 / 1e18 + 0.2e18 = 1111
        if (creditAmountIn == maxCredit) {
            // no credit fractionalization

            fees = getSwapFee(state, maxCashAmountOut, tenor); //@audit 10% of 1111 = 111

            if (fees > maxCashAmountOut) {
                revert Errors.NOT_ENOUGH_CASH(maxCashAmountOut, fees);
            }

            cashAmountOut = maxCashAmountOut - fees; //@audit 1111 - 111 = 1000
```
* fees = 111
* cashAmountOut = 1000

From this we can see that when the cash recieved is exactly the same i.e. 1000, 
credit amount to pay back is also exactly the same i.e. 1334,
but the fees are different, 100 and 111.

And this is because there is miscalculation of fees when ```exactAmountIn = false```.

With the same credit = 1334, try more examples such as a lender early exiting by selling 1334 of his credit and we will get the same results i.e. 111 as fees.


### Estimation of how much fees would actually be loss using deploy.sol values:
```
at 0.5% swap fee and tenor = 5 years

amount                              fees loss        USD $ price        
(in USDC e6 precision)
1000                                641025           $ 0.64
10000                               6410256          $ 6.41 
100000                              64102564         $ 64.10
1000000                             641025641        $ 641.02

we have to note here that the borrower doesn't need to necessarily borrow 10000000 for the protocol to loss $641, but with every small borrows the fee loss is accumulating.
...
```
And since the fee is not fixed and can be changed by the protcol using ```updateConfig```, 
If the protocol decides to increase the fees to 1%, amount loss will be doubled at 1.5% it will be trippled and so on. Hence, reporting this as a high severity. 

## Tools Used
manual 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Change the fees calculation in [```getCreditAmountIn```](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/AccountingLibrary.sol#L249C13-L256C109) to:

```diff
if (cashAmountOut == maxCashAmountOut) {
            // no credit fractionalization

            creditAmountIn = maxCredit;
-           fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT);
+           fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT - swapFeePercent);
        } else if (cashAmountOut < maxCashAmountOutFragmentation) {
            // credit fractionalization

            creditAmountIn = Math.mulDivUp(
                cashAmountOut + state.feeConfig.fragmentationFee, PERCENT + ratePerTenor, PERCENT - swapFeePercent
            );
-            fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT) + state.feeConfig.fragmentationFee;
+            fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT - swapFeePercent) - state.feeConfig.fragmentationFee;
```



## Assessed type

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/Size.sol#L177-L186


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

A trader(credit seller) who lends with a higher interest rate and early exit using ```executeBuyCreditMarket``` with lower interest rate to earn profit could be forced to borrow incase he liquidate a position.

The trader pays interest + swap fees and also got exposed to being underwater and liquidated, when his intention was to never borrow but instead sell his credit. 

## Proof of Concept
A lender can sell his credit to another lender to exit position earlier. And this can be done in two ways, ```SellCreditMarket``` or ```BuyCreditMarket```. Incase there is no order the seller likes then he puts up an order to sell his credit and wait for another lender to call ```BuyCreditMarket``` with his Id. 

The problem here is in the fact that to sell credit through ```BuyCreditMarket``` the seller needs to put up a ```borrowOffer``` which is the same struct used by a borrower. 
```javascript
} else {
            DebtPosition storage debtPosition = state.getDebtPositionByCreditPositionId(params.creditPositionId);
            creditPosition = state.getCreditPosition(params.creditPositionId);

            borrower = creditPosition.lender;
            tenor = debtPosition.dueDate - block.timestamp;
        }

        uint256 ratePerTenor = state.data.users[borrower].borrowOffer.getRatePerTenor(
            VariablePoolBorrowRateParams({
                variablePoolBorrowRate: state.oracle.variablePoolBorrowRate,
                variablePoolBorrowRateUpdatedAt: state.oracle.variablePoolBorrowRateUpdatedAt,
                variablePoolBorrowRateStaleRateInterval: state.oracle.variablePoolBorrowRateStaleRateInterval
            }),
            tenor
        );
```

This alone is not a probem because if try to let the seller borrow it will revert because the seller(trader) does not have any collateral at this point. 
```javascript
    function buyCreditMarket(BuyCreditMarketParams calldata params) external payable override(ISize) whenNotPaused {
        state.validateBuyCreditMarket(params);
        uint256 amount = state.executeBuyCreditMarket(params);
        if (params.creditPositionId == RESERVED_ID) {
            state.validateUserIsNotBelowOpeningLimitBorrowCR(params.borrower);
        }
```
```validateUserIsNotBelowOpeningLimitBorrowCR``` will revert the transaction in this case.


But if the seller wants to earn by liquidating a position(which is very likely considering the user(trader)'s intention is to earn) then this attack becomes possible.

After liquidation he recieves a collateral from the liquidated psoition:
```state.data.collateralToken.transferFrom(debtPosition.borrower, msg.sender, liquidatorProfitCollateralToken);```

Now, since he has collateral the ```borrowOffer``` he put up for selling his credit can be used to make him borroww instead of buying his credit. 
This can be done by calling ```buyCreditMarket``` with RESERVED_ID and the trader's address as the borrower. 
All checks will pass because the same offer struct is used. 

The trader's whose intention was to sell his credit is now forced to borrow and pay interest and also swap fees. 


Example:
* Bob is a trader that earns profit by buying credit(lending with higher rate) and selling it early with lower rate.
* Bob's collaterlaTokens = 0, credit = 1000000
* Bob finds no order that interest him to ```executeSellCreditMarket```.
* So bob puts up a ```borrowOffer``` since thats the only way to sell his credit so that a lender migh match him through ```buyCreditMarket```. 
* Bob finds a profitable liquidation so he wants to earn extra profit from it.
* Bob executes liquidation and he receives collateralTokens back.
* Bob's borrowOffer suddenly becomes a two way offer, one for selliing his credit and one for letting him borrow tokens.
* Alice quickly execute ```BuyCreditMarket``` with Bob as the borrower but not to buy his credit, instead to let him borrow. Alice doesn't necessarily need to be a malicious attacker here. Alice might simply think bob wants to borrow and executed that and it is valid.
* Suppose the amount made to borrow was 1000 and interest was 10% then Bob loss 100 + swap fees, he will be liquidated if he doesn't repay, paying more.

* Since borrowOffers are never cleared even after fulfilled, it increases the likelyhood of this issue. 

Reporting this as a medium severity because, every action Bob and Alice does here is a valid action and since it is not a know issue that Bob could be made to borrow incase he liquidate a position while having an open borrowOffer to sell credit(with an intention to sell existing credit not to borrow tokens).

## Tools Used
manual 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
consider using a different struct order for selling credit when a lender sells his credit using ```executeBuyCreditMarket```.

The same way we have functions to put up a loanOffer and borrrowOffer, there should be another one for credit owner to put an offer that indicates they want to sell their credit. Which is separated from the borrowOffer, so that a seller with an intention to sell credit does not need to use borrowOffer.






## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/Size.sol#L208-L220


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

* Lenders losing funds due to unliquidatable positions. Not only interest but including the principal.
* Borrowers with intention to repay gets unfairly liquidated loosing his collateral.

## Proof of Concept
When liquidation is done the caller repays using the ```borrowATokens```:
```
state.data.collateralToken.transferFrom(debtPosition.borrower, msg.sender, liquidatorProfitCollateralToken);
```
And to get the borrowATokens the liquidator must first deposit USDC through ```deposit``` which will deposit it to the variablePool and mint ```borrowATokens``` to the user.
```javascript
    function depositUnderlyingBorrowTokenToVariablePool(State storage state, address from, address to, uint256 amount)
        external
    {
        state.data.underlyingBorrowToken.safeTransferFrom(from, address(this), amount); 

        IAToken aToken =
            IAToken(state.data.variablePool.getReserveData(address(state.data.underlyingBorrowToken)).aTokenAddress); 

        uint256 scaledBalanceBefore = aToken.scaledBalanceOf(address(this)); 

        state.data.underlyingBorrowToken.forceApprove(address(state.data.variablePool), amount);
        state.data.variablePool.supply(address(state.data.underlyingBorrowToken), amount, address(this), 0);

        uint256 scaledAmount = aToken.scaledBalanceOf(address(this)) - scaledBalanceBefore;

        state.data.borrowAToken.mintScaled(to, scaledAmount);
    }
```
We also know that when this variable pool is paused withdraws are not allowed.

Suppose this pool is paused or inactive, the positions that are overdue or underwater cannot be liquidated leading to lenders not recieving their repayments on time or not at all. 

Example;
* There are 5 lenders each of them with 1000 borrowATokens
* four of them have lended to borrowers who withdrew the tokens to USDC 
* Now, there is only 1000 borrowATokens. 
* Liquidity pool becomes inactive
* loans are overdue or underwater, and becomes liquidatable 
* now since there is no other mechanism to mint borrowATokens, 1000 is not enough to liquidate all of the 4 borrowers, with the interest included it becomes more.

Lenders will never be paid back even with overdue loans, lenders only hope is that the collateral ratio decreases so that they can recieve atleast some collateralTokens even if they have to lose funds, or for aave to unpause the pool.

In this case, the protocol bots might have some reserves it is not guarrantee that they will always have enough ```borrowATokens``` at all times. This can be confirmed from [known issues]():

```The insurance fund (out of scope for this project) may not be able to make all lenders whole, may be unfair, and may be manipulated```.


#### There are actually two opposite outcomes of this issue;
The other one is a borrower willing to repay will also need borrowATokens. 
So, he may become unfairly liquidated;

Example:
* 5 lenders with 1000 borrowATokens each
* only 1000 is borrowed by Bob, and he withdraws it to USDC.
* 4000 borrowAToken remains 
* variable pool becomes inactive
* during inactivity of the pool, bob's loan is almost overdue or undercollateralized
* bob wants to repay, but since liquidity pool is paused bob cannot get enough tokens to repay the debt
* Now, bob gets unfairly liquidated, even when he intended to repay the loan. 

So, for the borrowers who has withdrawn their borrowATokens to USDC(since that is the purpose of borrowing) when the variable pool suddenly becomes inactive, they will not be allowed to repay it and risk being liquidated. The risk increases if the dueDate is near. 


## Tools Used
manual 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
create a separate ```liquidationWhenVariablePoolInactive``` and ```repayWhenVariablePoolInactive``` functions ;
* the functions should check that the pool is indeed inactive or paused
* the functions should repay directly in USDC
* implement a boolean ```repaidDuringInactivePool``` variable in the ```debtPosition```, and set it to true when it is repaid during pool inactive.
* implement an if statement in the normal ```claim``` function that will instead send USDC directly to the lender address if this ```repaidDuringInactivePool``` is true.
* other accounting mechanisms should stay the same.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/Size.sol#L178-L195


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Unwilling users can be forced to borrow unwithdrawable USDC, which defeats the whole purpose of borrowing.And made to pay interests on it plus exposing him to borrow risks like overDue or underwater.

Useless as in not convertible to USDC, for borrowers who wants USDC. 



## Proof of Concept
As mentioned in the [known issues](https://code4rena.com/audits/2024-06-size#top:~:text=If%20the%20Variable%20Pool%20(Aave%20v3)%20fails%20to%20supply%20or%20withdraw%20for%20any%20reason%2C%20such%20as%20supply%20caps%2C%20Size%27s%20deposit%20and%20withdraw%20may%20be%20prevented) and the [comments](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/CapsLibrary.sol#L60C3-L64C58), ```szaUSDC``` cannot be withdrawn to ```USDC``` incase the liquidity pool is paused, and this is a know risk that should be taken by users who are willing to hold it. 

This means that borrowers who wants to borrow for the sake of withdrawing USDC has to clear their borrowOffer incase variable pool becomes inactive or paused.
But these users can be frontrunned by malicious borrowAToken holders to let them borrow unwithdrawable USDC.  


Example:
* Bob wants to borrow 1000 USDC, so he puts up a borrowOffer and collateral
* Bob's offer is not yet matched
* variable pool suddenly becomes unavailable(inactive, paused, frozen).
* Bob doesn't want to borrow anymore since he wont be able to withdraw USDC, so its useless to him.
* So Bob decides to clear his offer or withdraw his collateral.
* Alice has 1000 borrowATokens, since the token is currently worthless alice wants to get rid of it 
* Alice frontruns bob, by calling lending him 1000 borrowATokens
* Bob's collateral is now locked, Bob also cannot repay because 1000 is not enough to repay the futureValue which includes the interest. 
* Bob can only repay or withdraw when the pool is active.
* Alice sucessfully got rid of borrowATokens and by the time Bob repays the pool is available and borrowATokens becomes worth again.  

Since Alice had been holding the borrowATokens and earning interest way before the pool was paused, Alice should be the one taking the risk, not Bob who enters post unavailabilty of the pool. 
i.e. a user who has been in the protocol since the variable pool was active can transfer his risk to a new user who is just entering, post pool inactivity. 
 

And since borrowAToken becomes worthless, and when the pool will become available again is unknown, there is a very high chance for borrowATokens holders to perform this attack.




*There can also be another attack path where the attacker directly frontruns the aave's call to pause or freeze the pool, instead of the borrower's transaction. The same impact can be achieved this way.*

## Tools Used
manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
implement a boolean ```allowDuringPoolInactivity``` variable in the [```BorrowOffer```](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/OfferLibrary.sol#L17C1-L21C2) so that a user can choose to accept borrowing even when pool is unavailable or choose to not accept the borrowATokens when pool is unavailable. 
And whenever a borrow market is to be executed during unavailable pool, check this variable and execute the borrow if true else revert. 


The second attack path can be completely avoided if aave decides to do update pool calls through flashbots, but still the first one exist.
And if aave doesn't use flash bots, then there is no immediate mitigation but size protocol could find a way to closely work with aave team so that they get notified off-chain atleast 5 minutes before pool gets paused/frozen. That way size can pause borrows through flashbots and unpause them after 5 minutes.



## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/BuyCreditMarket.sol#L67-L72
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/RiskLibrary.sol#L89-L96


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
"considering a credit maturing at T if it is liquidated at t < T and therefore it is claimable at t then if the credit is also available for sale somebody can buy it at a discount depending on T-t and claim it immediately, resulting in an arbitrage

for this reason, claimable credit is non-transferable." according to docs.

Claimable credit is transferable

The vulnerability arises when creditors hold unclaimed credit on a position while debtors, cleared in that context, are in liquidation elsewhere in the protocol. This exposes creditors to risks such as losing Aave token bearing interest and interest depending on the remaining tenor. The preconditions are that the credit should be claimable, the debtor should be in liquidation in any position in the protocol and the creditor should not have disabled credit transfer.

## Proof of Concept

The key issue is that the LoanStatus check is specific to the credit position, while the borrower's solvency is determined by their overall solvency within the entire protocol.


   /// @notice Check if a credit position is transferrable
    /// @dev A credit position is transferrable if the loan is ACTIVE and the related borrower is not underwater
    /// @param state The state
    /// @param creditPositionId The credit position ID
    /// @return True if the credit position is transferrable, false otherwise
    function isCreditPositionTransferrable(State storage state, uint256 creditPositionId)
        internal
        view
        returns (bool)
    {
        return state.getLoanStatus(creditPositionId) == LoanStatus.ACTIVE
            && !isUserUnderwater(state, state.getDebtPositionByCreditPositionId(creditPositionId).borrower);
    }


The conditional statement above does not correctly handle cases where a loan has been repaid, but the borrower is still underwater with another lender. In such cases, it returns true when, according to the documented notes, it should return false.

For example, Alice hasn't claimed her credit from Bob, who repaid early. Later, Bob goes into liquidation with Tom from another loan. During this period, Mike, an arbitrager, buys Alice's credit and profits from the interest between the tenor and Aave's interest-bearing token. Alice is unhappy because she lost some profit.

Alice.getLoanStatus(creditPositionId)==LoanStatus.Active ---> False 
!isUserUnderwater(Borrower=Bob, insolvent) ----> False

Therefore False && False == True
(As notes say and in practice true means credit is transferable)

## Tools Used

Static Analysis

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Send Tokens straight to lender after repay or liquidation, instead of holding them in contract.
Mark creditPosition as not transferable during debt repayment or liquidation function as there is check if credit is transferable during validatBuyCreditMarket() function.

Source:

1. Size Credit Technical Documentation, https://docs.size.credit/technical-docs/contracts/2.2-loans

Notes (Other Attack Vectors besides Arbitrage):

+ Borrowers can exploit this flaw to evade fees as well, especially on long-term or large loans they expect to repay early.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
### `latestRoundData()` Call May Result Stale
The contract calls out to a Chainlink oracle receiving the latestRoundData(). If there is a problem with Chainlink starting a new round and finding consensus on the new value for the oracle (e.g. Chainlink nodes abandon the oracle, chain congestion, vulnerability/attacks on the chainlink system) consumers of this contract may continue using outdated stale or incorrect data (if oracles are unable to submit no new round is started).Take a look at the [Chainlink documentation](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/price-feeds/historical-data#getrounddata-return-values)

```solidity
Path: ./src/oracle/PriceFeed.sol

66:            (, int256 answer, uint256 startedAt,,) = sequencerUptimeFeed.latestRoundData();	// @audit-issue

86:        (, int256 price,, uint256 updatedAt,) = aggregator.latestRoundData();	// @audit-issue
```


## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Implement comprehensive checks to validate the freshness of the data returned by Chainlink's `latestRoundData()` in your smart contracts. This includes verifying the timestamp of the latest round against a permissible time window to ensure the data's relevance and accuracy. Additionally, consider using Chainlink's `getRoundData()` function with specific round IDs for historical data checks and to verify data continuity. Add the following checks:
```solidity
...
( roundId, rawPrice, , updateTime, answeredInRound ) = AggregatorV3Interface(XXXXX).latestRoundData();
require(rawPrice > 0, "Chainlink price <= 0");
require(updateTime != 0, "Incomplete round");
require(answeredInRound >= roundId, "Stale price");
...
```

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

The testing was performed using the Foundry framework, particularly focusing on the amountToWad function.

Audit Scope Files
src/libraries/Math.sol (Library implementation)
test/libraries/Maths.t.sol (Test cases for the library)

amountToWad was thoroughly tested to ensure its reliability in converting amounts with different decimal places to a fixed decimal format.

The amountToWad function in the Math library is intended to convert token amounts with arbitrary decimal places into an equivalent representation in Wad format (18 decimal places). However, the function failed the unit test when trying to convert an amount of 1000 with 5 decimals to Wad, returning 10^16 instead of the expected 10^11.

This incorrect conversion could lead to significant financial discrepancies in applications relying on this function for financial calculations involving token amounts.

The amountToWad function is implemented as follows:
```sol
function amountToWad(uint256 amount, uint8 decimals) internal pure returns (uint256) {
    return amount * 10 ** (18 - decimals);
}
```

This implementation assumes that multiplying by 10 ** (18 - decimals) will always convert the amount correctly to Wad format. The failure in the test case indicates a misapplication of the decimal conversion logic.
## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

Test Case Output
Test Case: testAmountToWad()
Input: amount = 1000, decimals = 5
Expected Output: 100000000000
Actual Output: 10000000000000000
Error Message: "The amountToWad calculation did not return the expected result."

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/Size.sol#L110-L117


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

A critical vulnerability was identified in the updateConfig function of the Size.sol smart contract. The function is intended to be protected by a role check (onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE)), which is supposed to limit the execution of the function to users with the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE. However, due to a misconfiguration or potential oversight in assigning or validating these roles, an unauthorised address could potentially invoke this function. This could lead to unauthorised changes in the contract's configuration settings, potentially affecting fee structures, operational parameters, or other critical settings. The pause function is also called by the unauthorised address.

## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

The updateConfig function is designed to update configuration parameters of the contract. Here is an example where an unauthorised address (0xbEEF) is able to call updateConfig due to incorrect role assignment or validation:

1. Deploy the Size contract and incorrectly set up the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE or simulate an attack where DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is compromised.
2. An unauthorised address (e.g., 0xbEEF) uses the vm.prank feature in a test environment to simulate calling from an admin address.
3. The unauthorised address calls updateConfig to change the swapFeeAPR configuration to an arbitrary value such as 999.
4. This change reflects in the contract state, proving that the protection mechanism is not effective.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/SelfLiquidate.sol#L59-L70
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/LoanLibrary.sol#L170-L186
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/LoanLibrary.sol#L148-L161


# Vulnerability details



## Impact
Lender/SelfLiquidator receives less collateral from borrower than expected due to extra flooring done to calculate the `ProRataAssignedCollateral`.

## Proof of Concept

In the `executeSelfLiquidate` we are passing `creditPosition` to calculate the `ProRataAssignedCollateral` which is then transferred to selfLiquidator.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/SelfLiquidate.sol#L59-L70

```solidity
function executeSelfLiquidate(State storage state, SelfLiquidateParams calldata params) external {
....
=>        uint256 assignedCollateral = state.getCreditPositionProRataAssignedCollateral(creditPosition);
....
}   
```

Inorder to calculate the the `proRataAssignedCollateral` protocol is first calculating the assignedCollateral to that debt Position from the total debt that the borrower has and then again calculating the assigned credit to that particular lender of that debtPosition.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/LoanLibrary.sol#L170-L186
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/LoanLibrary.sol#L148-L161

   `assignedCollateral` = floor(collateralToken * debtPosition.futureValue/debt)
   `proRataAssignedCollateral` = floor(`assignedCollateral`*credit/debtPosition.futureValue)

So the final `proRataAssignedCollateral` can result to a less amount since flooring is done more than once.

Instead , we can just do `proRataAssignedCollateral` = floor(collateralToken*credit/debt).

because, (collateralToken * debtPosition.futureValue/debt) * (credit/debtPosition.futureValue) = collateralToken*credit/debt

This can be proved theoretically.

suppose there 2 lenders `A` and `B` for a debtPosition `X` and the borrower of the debtPosition has one more debtPosition `Y` which has a lender with credit `C`.

so some of all the credits should be equal to total debt.
=> creditAx + creditBx + creditCy = debtPostionX.futurevalue  +  debtPostionY.futurevalue = debt.
=> Equivalent share of lender can be calculated directly using (credit of that lender / debt );

floor(collateralToken*creditAx / debt ) + floor(collateralToken*creditBx / debt ) + floor(collateralToken*creditCy / debt ) <= collateralTOken.

since, creditAx + creditBx + creditCy = debt



## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
We can replace the above caluclation by this equation
```solidity
uint256 debt = state.data.debtToken.balanceOf(debtPosition.borrower);
uint256 collateral = state.data.collateralToken.balanceOf;
uint256 creditPositionCredit = creditPosition.credit;(debtPosition.borrower);
proRataAssignedCollateral = Math.mulDivDown(collateral, creditPositionCredit, debt);  
```


## Assessed type

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Compensate.sol#L42-L101
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/Size.sol#L247-L251


# Vulnerability details


## Impact
Borrower cannot save himself from liquidation by paying partial debt using compensate due to the underwater check. This issue is very relevant in Multicalls. 

## Proof of Concept

A borrower can use compensate to create  a new debtPosition/creditPosition pair to repay the new `debtPosition.futureValue` inorder to avoid ffrom the liquidation. This is done by passing the `RESERVE_ID` to `creditPositionToCompensateId`.

Borrower can also compensate the some credit of the existing `creditPositiontoCompensate` of his to the lender whom he needs to repay irrespective of whether the msg.sender is underwater or not.(borrower for `creditPositionToCompensateId` is checked)
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Compensate.sol#L42-L101.

But after executing the `compensate` we are checking whether the sender/borrower is underwater. This check only works if the borrower is compensating his current creditPOsition to repay.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/Size.sol#L247-L251

function compensate(CompensateParams calldata params) external payable override(ISize) whenNotPaused {
    state.validateCompensate(params);
    state.executeCompensate(params);
=>  state.validateUserIsNotUnderwater(msg.sender);
}

Suppose  if borrower, whose `collateralRatio` went below `minimumCRLiquidation` ,  decided to repay the lender by doing partial liquidation. 
the flow will be   `compensate` -> `repay`

When the `executeCompensate` is executed a new credit-debtPosition is created where the borrower is the same msg.sender.

But the borrower's `debt` balance wouldnt get changed untill he `repay` the created debtPosition.

So the underwater check will revert and wouldnt allow the borrower to repay.


## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
```solidity
if(`CompensateParams.creditPositionToCompensateId` != `RESERVE_ID`)
state.validateUserIsNotUnderwater(msg.sender); 
else{
    /*check the CR of the sender > PERCENT. else sender can prevent lender from doing selfLiquidation by to frontrunning compensate divide the debtPosition to smaller futureVlaue.*/
}
```

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Compensate.sol#L106-L156
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/AccountingLibrary.sol#L153-L158


# Vulnerability details


## Impact
msg.sender/attacker can fill all the debtPosition and creditPosition slots available with the same data without facing any loss, using Compensate.

## Proof of Concept

When `CompensateParams.creditPositionToCompensateId == RESERVE_ID` , the sender/borrower can execute `executeCompensate` with `CompensateParams.amount == creditPositionToRepay.credit`.

In this case a new creditPosition and debtPosition is created with `futureValue = amountToCompensate = creditPositionToRepay.credit`.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/Compensate.sol#L106-L156

```solidity
if (params.creditPositionToCompensateId == RESERVED_ID) {
            creditPositionToCompensate = state.createDebtAndCreditPositions({
                lender: msg.sender,
                borrower: msg.sender,
                futureValue: amountToCompensate,
                dueDate: debtPositionToRepay.dueDate
            }); 
}
```

> That means the sender can create `new exact copies `of the already existing `creditPositionToRepay` and `debtPositionToRepay` , before reducing their futureValue and credit respectively to `0`  using `reduceDebtAndCredit`.
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/AccountingLibrary.sol#L153-L158

Also , there are no changes in the state of any users or positions except the protocols storage is getting utilised inefficiantly.

Sender/attacker can go on and execute multiple similar transactions (type(uint256).max / 2)  and grief the protocol.


## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps

In case of `CompensateParams.creditPositionToCompensateId == RESERVE_ID` protocol shouldnt allow compensate if `CompensateParams.amount == creditPositionToRepay.credit` by adding this validation in `validateCompensate()` .

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

A malicious user can decrease a victim's `position.credit` amount. This can be critical and cause significant losses for users.

## Proof of Concept

### Scenario:
1. A malicious actor observes the victim's transaction, which at some point calls the `createCreditPosition` function.
2. The malicious actor then creates a similar transaction using the same `exitCreditPositionId` but with a lower `credit` amount.
3. The attacker calculates the difference between the victim's credit and their own credit, ensuring that the remaining credit is greater than the minimum required credit to be successful to be sure this check will succeed `state.validateMinimumCredit(creditPosition.credit);`.
4. Finally, the attacker sends the transaction, which reduces the victim's `credit` by the amount the attacker specified in the function.

### Example:
1. Alice creates a position with `id = 1` and `credit = 100`.
2. Bob creates a position with `id = 1` and `credit = 90` (assuming the minimum credit is 10).
3. Bob's transaction reduces Alice's credit by 90, leaving Alice with a credit of 10.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Add a check to ensure that `msg.sender` is also the credit lender:

```javascript
require(msg.sender == creditPosition.lender);
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/actions/SellCreditMarket.sol#L168-L182
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/AccountingLibrary.sol#L250-L256


# Vulnerability details

 ## Impact
- The incorrect calculation of `creditAmountIn` results in lenders receiving more credit than they should, while borrowers receive less `cash`. This discrepancy, although small it can become higher with higher swap fees or larger transaction amounts, leading to financial imbalances and potential exploitation of the protocol.
 ## Proof of Concept
- - In the Size protocol, selling a credit market involves a user (borrower) specifying an amount . This amount can represent either the cash they will receive immediately (`cashAmountOut`) or the credit they will repay at maturity (`creditAmountIn`). The user sets the `exactAmountIn` boolean flag to `true` if the amount represents `creditAmountIn` and `false` if it represents `cashAmountOut`.
```js
    function executeSellCreditMarket(State storage state, SellCreditMarketParams calldata params) external returns (uint256 cashAmountOut) {
        // some code ....

        uint256 creditAmountIn;
        uint256 fees;

    >>  if (params.exactAmountIn) {
            creditAmountIn = params.amount;

    >>      (cashAmountOut, fees) = state.getCashAmountOut({
                creditAmountIn: creditAmountIn,
                maxCredit: params.creditPositionId == RESERVED_ID ? creditAmountIn : creditPosition.credit,
                ratePerTenor: ratePerTenor,
                tenor: tenor
            });} else {
    >>       cashAmountOut = params.amount;
    >>      (creditAmountIn, fees) = state.getCreditAmountIn({
                cashAmountOut: cashAmountOut,
                maxCashAmountOut: params.creditPositionId == RESERVED_ID ? cashAmountOut : Math.mulDivDown(creditPosition.credit, PERCENT - state.getSwapFeePercent(tenor), PERCENT + ratePerTenor),
                maxCredit: params.creditPositionId == RESERVED_ID ? Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, PERCENT + ratePerTenor, PERCENT - state.getSwapFeePercent(tenor)) : creditPosition.credit,
                ratePerTenor: ratePerTenor,
                tenor: tenor
            });
        }
    }
```
- - In `sellCreditMarket` , the borrower (as `msg.sender`) is responsible for paying the swap fees *since the borrower always pays these fees*. If there is a split on the credit, the borrower also pays the fragmentation fees because they are the caller and the one causing the credit split.

- Since borrower pays all the fees , and lender isn't paying any ,the invariant to be maintained is that the credit amount lender will get at maturity should be calculated as:
- 
  \[
  \text{credit} = (\text{cashAmountOut} + \text{fees}) \times (1 + \text{rate})
  \]

  This means that the credit amount (the amount the borrower pays the lender at maturity) should be equal to the  amount the lender pays( cashAmountOut plus all applicable fees), multiplied by the rate .
- we're interested in when `exactAmountIn` set to `false` means the borrower specifies `cashAmountOut`. The protocol calculates `creditAmountIn` and applicable fees using the `getCreditAmountIn` function,The issue arises when there is a split of credit(lender exit), and fragmentation fees are applied. The current calculation for `creditAmountIn` is incorrect : 
```js
 else if (cashAmountOut < maxCashAmountOutFragmentation) {

   >>       creditAmountIn = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut + state.feeConfig.fragmentationFee, PERCENT + ratePerTenor, PERCENT - swapFeePercent);
            fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT) + state.feeConfig.fragmentationFee;
        } 
```

- The current calculation for `creditAmountIn` is:
\[
\text{creditAmountIn} = \frac{(\text{cashAmountOut} + \text{fragmentationFee}) \times (1 + \text{ratePerTenor})}{1 - \text{swapFeePercent}}
\]
- The current formula attempts to account for the fragmentation fee and the rate per tenor but incorrectly divides by \(1 - \text{swapFeePercent}\).
- This results in an inflated `creditAmountIn`, causing the lender to receive more credit than they should and the borrower to receive less cash than they should.
---
- The correct formula should add the swap fee to the cash amount out and fragmentation fee before applying the rate per tenor.
- This ensures that the borrower pays the correct amount of fees and the lender receives the correct amount of credit.
- The correct calculation should be:
\[
\text{creditAmountIn} = (\text{cashAmountOut} + \text{fragmentationFee} + (\text{cashAmountOut} \times \text{swapFeePercent})) \times (1 + \text{ratePerTenor})
\]

#### Example

Let's use an example to illustrate the issue:

- **Given**:
  - `cashAmountOut` = 1000e6
  - `fragmentationFees` = 5e6
  - `swapFees` = 0.02 (2% for 4 years)
  - `ratePerTenor` = 50% (for 4 years)

##### Incorrect Calculation

Using the incorrect formula:
\[
\text{creditAmountIn} = \frac{(\text{cashAmountOut} + \text{fragmentationFees}) \times (1 + \text{ratePerTenor})}{1 - \text{swapFeePercent}}
\]
\[
\text{creditAmountIn} = \frac{(1000e6 + 5e6) \times 1.5}{0.98} = \frac{1507.5e6}{0.98} \approx 1537.76e6
\]

##### Correct Calculation

First, calculate the total amount the lender will pay:
```js
    // fees calculated as : 
    fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT) + state.feeConfig.fragmentationFee;
    // lender pays : 
    state.data.borrowAToken.transferFrom(params.lender, msg.sender, cashAmountOut);
    state.data.borrowAToken.transferFrom(params.lender, state.feeConfig.feeRecipient, fees);
```

\[
\text{Total Amount Paid by Lender} = \text{cashAmountOut} + \text{fragmentationFees} + (\text{cashAmountOut} \times \text{swapFeePercent})
\]
\[
\text{Total Amount Paid by Lender} = 1000e6 + 5e6 + (1000e6 \times 0.02) = 1000e6 + 5e6 + 20e6 = 1025e6
\]

Next, calculate the actual amount the lender should receive as credit:
\[
\text{Actual Credit Amount} = \text{Total Amount Paid by Lender} \times (1 + \text{ratePerTenor})
\]
\[
\text{Actual Credit Amount} = 1025e6 \times 1.5 = 1537.5e6
\]

##### Comparison

- **Incorrect Calculation**: `creditAmountIn` = 1537.76e6
- **Correct Calculation**: `Actual Credit Amount` = 1537.5e6

The lender is getting more credit than they should:
\[
1537.76e6 - 1537.5e6 = 0.26e6
\]

This discrepancy shows that the lender is receiving more credit than the amount they paid multiplied by \(1 + \text{ratePerTenor}\), which means the borrower is getting less cash than they should.

- `Notice` The amount of discrepancy in this example is not significant. However, since the swap fees can be increased by the admin, the discrepancy can become larger. Additionally, the discrepancy scales with the amount involved—the higher the amount, the greater the discrepancy.
 ## Tools Used
 manual review , foundry testing 
 ## Recommended Mitigation Steps 
 - make this changes in [getCreditAmountIn](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-size/blob/8850e25fb088898e9cf86f9be1c401ad155bea86/src/libraries/AccountingLibrary.sol#L228-L263) function : 
```Diff
    function getCreditAmountIn(State storage state, uint256 cashAmountOut, uint256 maxCashAmountOut, uint256 maxCredit, uint256 ratePerTenor, uint256 tenor)
        internal
        view
        returns (uint256 creditAmountIn, uint256 fees)
    {
       // prev code ..

        else if (cashAmountOut < maxCashAmountOutFragmentation) {
 
-           creditAmountIn = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut + state.feeConfig.fragmentationFee, PERCENT + ratePerTenor, PERCENT - swapFeePercent);
            fees = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut, swapFeePercent, PERCENT) + state.feeConfig.fragmentationFee;
+           creditAmountIn = Math.mulDivUp(cashAmountOut + fees, PERCENT + ratePerTenor, PERCENT);
           
        } 
        // same code ...
    }
```
